# Book Notes - An Elegant Puzzle

**Book:** *An Elegant Puzzle: Systems of Engineering Management*, Will Larson
**Read:** August 2026, a chapter a night, mostly on the couch after KYC calls
**Rating:** 8/10. Uneven, but the org-sizing chapters are worth the whole book.

## Why now

The post-close hiring plan is going to take us from 31 engineers to something over 40 in nine months. I've never designed an org at that size. Neither has anyone on the team. Also the VP Eng search started this week and I wanted to know what I'm hiring someone to do.

## What I'm keeping

### Team sizing: managers of 6-8, teams that can keep up with their own load

Larson's rule of thumb: teams of 6-8 per manager, and a team that can't keep up with its own on-call and maintenance load isn't a team, it's a liability.

Applied to us: Payments is effectively one team carrying ACH, KYC (until this week), reconciliation, the Pillar relationship, and every Rails money-moving job nobody else wants. That's not one team's load. Marcus has been the manager, the TL, and the on-call backstop. That's why he's tired ([[1on1 Marcus - 2026-08-26]]).

### The four states of a team

Falling behind, treading water, repaying debt, innovating. And the fixes differ: falling behind needs headcount, treading water needs reduced work in progress, repaying debt needs time, innovating needs slack.

- Payments: treading water, sliding toward falling behind.
- iOS: repaying debt (the refactor), with investing on top.
- Growth: honestly, close to innovating until we freeze experiments for the beta.
- Android: falling behind. We've under-hired it all year.

The useful thing is that "hire more" is only the right answer for one state.

### Migrations are the only scalable fix for tech debt

He argues you get out of debt by running migrations to completion, not by sprinkling fixes. We did this right with ACH and KYC. We're doing it wrong with the old Sidekiq jobs: half-migrated is worse than not started, because the old path still exists and someone can turn it back on.

Note to self: finish deleting the Sidekiq ACH code once the stability hold ends.

### Succession planning before you need it

"Plan for every important role to have a successor." We have no successor for Marcus on the Pillar relationship or on payments architecture. Sarah is the obvious start on the first ([[1on1 Sarah - 2026-08-05]]). Devon on the second.

## Where I disagree

He's comfortable with a lot more process than I am. Some of his templates would feel like bureaucracy to our team. I'd take his structures and use half of them.

## What I'm actually doing

1. Use the four-state model in the post-close hiring plan, so headcount goes where "falling behind" is true. (The Sep 21 hiring plan has 2 payments hires and an Android hire. Partly this book.)
2. Write down successors for the top five roles, including mine.
3. Ask both VP Eng finalists which state they think each of our teams is in. Good interview question: tells me whether they diagnose or prescribe. See [[VP Eng Search]].
